en: Hello.

en: I was at a wedding this weekend.

en: And it was in New York.
zh: 婚礼在纽约。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there were a bunch of trendy people there.
zh: 那里有一大堆时髦的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was talking to someone who I'd never met before.
zh: 我在和一个以前从没见过的人聊天。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I told him I was prepping for this presentation.

speaker: Unknown
en: And he was like, oh, that's cool.

speaker: Unknown

en: And I could just see his eyes glaze over.

speaker: Unknown
en: And he started looking behind me to find the next person to talk to.

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's so cool to actually be in a room full of people who actually want to hear about this stuff.
zh: 能真正待在一个满是真心想听这些内容的人的房间里，真是太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm very excited to be here.
zh: 所以我非常高兴能来到这里。

en: I am the co-founder of Conductor.

en: Has anyone here used Conductor?

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, nice, nice.

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, cool.
zh: 好，很酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for those who don't know, Conductor is a desktop app for managing a team of coding agents all at the same time.
zh: 那么，给不了解的人说一下，Conductor 是一个桌面应用，用于同时管理一个编码智能体团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: So instead of having a bunch of terminal windows for your cloud codes or your codexes or your whatever coding agent, you have one interface to manage them all.
zh: 所以，你不用再开一堆终端窗口来跑你的 cloud codes 或 codexes 或随便什么编码智能体，而是用一个界面来管理它们全部。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the really cool things about building Conductor has been that I've seen a lot of the best builders up close.
zh: 而构建 Conductor 过程中一件非常酷的事情是，我近距离看到了很多最出色的构建者。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've watched their workflow.
zh: 我观察过他们的工作流。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've seen how they work.
zh: 我看到他们是怎么工作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've seen the things they do do and the things that they avoid doing.
zh: 我看到他们做哪些事、以及避免做哪些事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I thought I would compile a bunch of the principles that I've seen the best engineers use and give them to you all.
zh: 所以我想把看到的最优秀的工程师们使用的一系列原则整理出来，分享给大家。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, here's what Conductor looks like.
zh: 那么，这就是 Conductor 的样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you guys see this?
zh: 你们能看到这个吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, nice.
zh: 好，很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, here's what Conductor looks like.
zh: 那么，这就是 Conductor 的样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And here are my principles for being the fastest builder in your organization.
zh: 这些是我关于如何成为你组织里最快的构建者的原则。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, let's start with number one, stay near the frontier.
zh: 那么，让我们从第一条开始，待在前沿附近。

speaker: Unknown
en: Staying near the frontier means you are always trying the latest things, basically the day they come out.
zh: 待在前沿附近意味着你总是在尝试最新的东西，基本上是它们发布的当天就去试。

speaker: Unknown
en: It means that when UltraCode comes out, you're trying it.
zh: 它意味着当 UltraCode 发布时，你会去试它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It means that when SlashGoal comes out, you're giving it a go.
zh: 它意味着当 SlashGoal 发布时，你会去试一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really important to stay near the frontier for a few reasons.
zh: 待在前沿附近非常重要，原因有几个。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you are doing your own startup, then staying near the frontier means that you will come up with lots of new ideas for what you should actually be building.
zh: 如果你在做自己的创业公司，那么待在前沿附近意味着你会想出很多关于你实际应该构建什么的新点子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this literally happened to us.
zh: 而这真实地发生在我们身上。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were building a totally different app called Chorus.
zh: 我们当时在做一个完全不同的应用，叫 Chorus。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we started using, we were such power users of Claude Code back in February of last year that we started building our whole workflow around Claude Code and we started cloning our repo five times and then we discovered work trees and then bit by bit we had built Conductor as an internal tool and we couldn't have figured that out if we weren't staying near the frontier.
zh: 但我们开始使用——去年二月我们是 Claude Code 的超级重度用户，以至于我们开始围绕 Claude Code 构建我们整个工作流，我们开始把仓库克隆五次，然后我们发现了 work trees，然后一点一点地，我们把 Conductor 作为内部工具构建了出来，如果我们不是待在前沿附近，我们不可能想出这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you're not doing a startup, you should be the person at your company who always knows what the latest workflows are.
zh: 而如果你不在做创业公司，你应该成为公司里那个永远知道最新工作流是什么的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It used to be that you could just kind of use your social graph and the information that was important about the best workflows to use would trickle down to you, but things just move way too fast now.
zh: 过去你大概可以只靠你的社交图谱，关于最佳工作流的重要信息会慢慢渗透到你这里，但现在 things 传播得太快了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're always going to be three to six months behind if you do that.
zh: 如果你那样做，你永远会落后三到六个月。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's very important to stay near the frontier.
zh: 所以待在前沿附近非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's an important word here, near.
zh: 而且这里有一个重要的词，附近。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is a danger if you are at the frontier.
zh: 如果你正处于前沿，是有危险的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can do what I call midwit memeing, where you're spending all of your time working on your workflow and not doing actual work.
zh: 你可能会陷入我所说的“中智梗图”，就是把所有时间都花在打磨工作流上，而不做实际的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so internally we've come up with a heuristic for this.
zh: 所以在内部我们为此想出了一个启发式方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: We call it don't beat the market.
zh: 我们称之为“不要跑赢市场”。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't try and beat the market.
zh: 不要试图跑赢市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: The concept here, the heuristic you should use when you're trying to decide if you're near the frontier or at the frontier and too deep into the latest trends is you should ask yourself,
zh: 这里的概念是，当你试图判断自己是在前沿附近，还是已经身处前沿、过于深入最新潮流时，应该使用的启发式方法是，你要问自己，

speaker: Unknown
en: Why isn't this workflow the default?
zh: 为什么这个工作流不是默认的?

speaker: Unknown
en: So, for example, when RALF loops were becoming a big thing, you should ask yourself, like, should I spend a ton of time optimizing my workflow to work with RALF loops?
zh: 举例来说,当 RALF 循环开始流行的时候,你应该问问自己,比如,我是否应该花大量时间优化我的工作流来配合 RALF 循环?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because
zh: 因为

speaker: Unknown
en: If route loops work for everyone, like if they are the default, then you probably should just wait for Anthropic or OpenAI or whatever to build the workflow into the default harness.
zh: 如果 route 循环对所有人都适用,比如如果它们是默认的,那你可能就应该等 Anthropic 或 OpenAI 或其他什么公司把这个工作流内置到默认的 harness 里。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can think of this as sort of like an efficient market hypothesis where unless you have like real alpha,
zh: 你可以把这理解成某种有效市场假说,除非你拥有真正的 alpha,

speaker: Unknown
en: You shouldn't be optimizing your workflow too much.
zh: 否则你不应该过度优化你的工作流。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I mean by real alpha is some kind of information about either your users or your code base that the models might not know about.
zh: 我说的真正的 alpha 是指某种关于你的用户或你的代码库的信息,模型可能不知道这些信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, an example for us is we're a chat app.
zh: 举个例子,对我们来说,我们是一个聊天应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have to render really long chats really quickly, and performance is important to us.
zh: 我们必须非常快速地渲染很长的聊天记录,性能对我们很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, we need to spend a lot of time optimizing our React queries to render the chats quickly.
zh: 所以,我们需要花很多时间优化我们的 React queries 来快速渲染聊天记录。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're willing to make sacrifices
zh: 而且我们愿意做出牺牲,

speaker: Unknown
en: and other parts of our code base to make that happen.
zh: 牺牲代码库的其他部分来实现这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, if you have some kind of alpha, it's like some kind of information about the app you're building that the models might not know about, then you should put time into the workflow.
zh: 所以,如果你有某种 alpha,也就是关于你正在构建的应用的某种模型可能不知道的信息,那你就应该把时间投入到工作流上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Otherwise, don't midwet meme, don't be the person who has an amazing Emacs setup but doesn't actually get stuff done.
zh: 否则,不要做那个梗里说的 midwet,不要成为那种有一套超棒的 Emacs 配置但实际上什么都干不成的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, three.
zh: 好,第三点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Create slot-free zones.
zh: 创建无 slop 区域。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, at Conductor, we have this term we call a slot-free zone.
zh: 在 Conductor,我们有一个术语叫无 slop 区域。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a slot-free zone is a part of the code base or a part of the app that requires really strict human review.
zh: 无 slop 区域是代码库的一部分或应用的一部分,需要非常严格的人工审查。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're actually, I think, a little bit unusual in this way.
zh: 实际上,我觉得我们在这方面有点不寻常。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot of people assume that we are
zh: 我想很多人以为我们是

speaker: Unknown
en: Pure token maxers, and we are ripping through 30,000 line PRs, but we're actually not.
zh: 纯粹的 token 最大化者,我们在猛改 3 万行的 PR,但其实我们不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're actually quite careful with certain parts of our codebase, and then very loose with other parts of our codebase.
zh: 实际上我们对代码库的某些部分非常谨慎,而对代码库的其他部分则非常宽松。

speaker: Unknown
en: The reason this is important is because if you are not careful about your slot-free zones, your codebase can get in a really...
zh: 这一点很重要的原因是,如果你对自己的无 slop 区域不够小心,你的代码库可能会陷入非常……

speaker: Unknown
en: Tricky spot.
zh: 棘手的境地。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this actually happened to us.
zh: 这确实发生在我们身上。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've had to rewrite our whole app a couple of times because we weren't careful about slot-free zones.
zh: 我们不得不把整个应用重写了好几次,就是因为我们对无 slop 区域不够小心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Specifically, we have a migrations file.
zh: 具体来说,我们有一个 migrations 文件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in our CI,
zh: 而在我们的 CI 中,

speaker: Unknown
en: Any change to the migrations file requires a human to review it.
zh: 对 migrations 文件的任何改动都需要一个人来审查。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also assume that anything written in Slack is slop-free.
zh: 我们还假定任何写在 Slack 里的东西都是无 slop 的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not written by the AI.
zh: 它不是 AI 写的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's written by a human.
zh: 它是人写的。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of our docs, our Claude MDs, all our skills, we put a ton of time into making them good.
zh: 我们所有的文档、我们的 Claude MD、我们所有的 skills,我们都花了大量时间把它们做好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is also something I've seen with all the best builders up close.
zh: 这也是我在近距离观察所有最优秀的构建者时看到的一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: They put an unusual amount of time into the Claude MD or their skill files.
zh: 他们会在 Claude MD 或他们的 skill 文件上投入多得不同寻常的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think another way that I've thought about this is if you had a new intern that was joining your company,
zh: 我想还有一个思考角度是:假如有一个新实习生要加入你的公司,

speaker: Unknown
en: And you had the opportunity to like whisper something in their ear every time they started working.
zh: 而你有机会在他们每次开始工作时在他们耳边低语一句话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like every day, any time they sat down, you could like whisper something in their ear.
zh: 比如每一天,每当他们坐下来,你都可以在他们耳边低语一句话。

speaker: Unknown
en: You would probably put a lot of thought into like what it is that you're whispering in their ear.
zh: 你大概会非常认真地思考要在他们耳边低语什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is what the CloudMD or AgentsMD is.
zh: 这就是 Claude MD 或 AgentsMD 的作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like information that gets loaded into the agent's context every time they start working.
zh: 它就像每次智能体开始工作时加载进其上下文的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you probably want to put a lot of thought into those.
zh: 所以你大概会想在这些内容上投入大量思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, four.
zh: 好,第四点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Feed the beast.
zh: 喂饱那头野兽。

speaker: Unknown
en: At Conductor we have an internal tool we call the Conductor Internal Agent.
zh: 在 Conductor 我们有一个内部工具,我们称之为 Conductor Internal Agent。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it is also known as the CIA.
zh: 它也被称为 CIA。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the CIA is basically the centralized database of everything that's happening in the organization.
zh: CIA 基本上就是一个集中式数据库,记录着组织里发生的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: So anytime a new Slack message gets sent,
zh: 所以每当有一条新的 Slack 消息发出,

speaker: Unknown
en: The CIA picks it up.
zh: CIA 都会接收到它。

speaker: Unknown
en: The CIA agent will see that a new message is sent in Slack.
zh: CIA 智能体会看到 Slack 里发出了一条新消息。

speaker: Unknown
en: It will pick it up and it will save it to a Postgres table.
zh: 它会把它捡起来并保存到 Postgres 表里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Any time a user has a bug request in Discord, the same thing happens.
zh: 每当用户在 Discord 里有一个 bug 请求时，同样的事情就会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: Any time we have a meeting, we are recording it and it goes into the CIA.
zh: 每当我们开会时，我们都会录音并把它传到 CIA。

speaker: Unknown
en: We call this Feed the Beast because you want to
zh: 我们把这叫做 Feed the Beast(喂饱野兽)，因为你想要

speaker: Unknown
en: For your agents to be effective in your company, you want them to have as much information and as much context as they can have about the way you guys specifically work.
zh: 要让你的智能体在你的公司里高效工作，你就要让它们尽可能多地拥有关于你们具体工作方式的信息和上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the best way to do that is by having a centralized place for all the information to go.
zh: 而做到这一点的最好方式，就是有一个集中的地方让所有信息汇聚过去。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this tweet sums it up pretty well.
zh: 我觉得这条推文总结得很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really effective to just put everything in a database and then give your agent a SQL tool and let it handle the rest.
zh: 把所有东西都放进一个数据库，然后给你的智能体一个 SQL 工具，让它处理剩下的部分，这真的很有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, next is Free Range Agents.
zh: 好的，下一个是 Free Range Agents(自由放养的智能体)。

speaker: Unknown
en: Give your agents a lot of space to play.
zh: 给你的智能体大量的空间去玩耍。

speaker: Unknown
en: Give them a sandbox that won't get killed, where they can explore your code base, where they can work on really hard tasks, where they know that they're not going to get shut down when you close your laptop lid.
zh: 给它们一个不会被杀掉的沙箱，在那里它们可以探索你的代码库，可以处理非常困难的任务，并且知道当你合上笔记本盖子时它们不会被关掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Give them opportunities to create more of themselves.
zh: 给它们创造更多自己的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Give them ways to collaborate with other agents and other humans.
zh: 给它们与其他智能体和其他人类协作的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think what's really interesting about free range agents and this concept and why this is important is the models are getting better and they are able to run for much longer and there are going to be many more of them.
zh: 我觉得自由放养智能体这个概念真正有意思、以及为什么它重要的地方在于，模型正在变得越来越好，它们能够运行更长的时间，而且它们的数量会多得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, if they are confined to your laptop, then they're not going to be nearly as effective as if they are free roaming.
zh: 所以，如果它们被限制在你的笔记本上，它们就不会像自由漫游时那样高效。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other thing that's important here is that once you give them a sandbox to play in that isn't confined to your laptop, there's a bunch of really cool stuff that you can build on top.
zh: 这里的另一个重要的点是，一旦你给它们一个不局限于你笔记本的沙箱，你就可以在上面构建很多非常酷的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have built some of those things into Conductor, and I'll give you a quick glimpse into some of those cool things.
zh: 我们已经把其中一些东西构建进了 Conductor，我会快速给你们看一眼其中一些很酷的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, this is Conductor.
zh: 那么，这就是 Conductor。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to make it a bit bigger.
zh: 我要把它放大一点。

en: And this is actually a new version of Conductor that is coming out this week, and it is centered around collaboration in the cloud.
zh: 这实际上是本周即将发布的一个新版本的 Conductor，它以云端协作为中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the thing I said was you need a sandbox for agents to play.
zh: 所以我刚才说的就是，你需要一个沙箱让智能体玩耍。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need a free-range agent.
zh: 你需要一个自由放养的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you'll notice that each workspace has a little cloud icon at the top, and I can click it and get information about the sandbox that the agent is running in.
zh: 所以你会注意到，每个工作区顶部都有一个小云朵图标，我可以点击它，获取智能体所运行沙箱的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what's awesome about this is I can close my laptop and the agents are going to keep running.
zh: 这最棒的地方是，我可以合上笔记本，智能体会继续运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: Up until basically this week, every task in Conductor was built on a Git Worktree, but now they're in a Cloud Sandbox.
zh: 基本上直到本周之前，Conductor 里的每个任务都是基于 Git Worktree 构建的，但现在它们处于云沙箱中。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are free range agents.

speaker: Unknown
en: But what's also really cool that we can build on top of Cloud is collaboration.
zh: 而我们可以在云之上构建的另一个非常酷的东西就是协作。

en: So, you'll see here, I'll make this even bigger.
zh: 那么，你们看这里，我把它放得更大一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's me.

speaker: Unknown
en: And here are a list of the things that I am working on.

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can see that I am in the conductor org.
zh: 你们可以看到我在 conductor 组织里。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if I scroll down, I can see what Caden's working on.
zh: 但如果我往下滚动，我可以看到 Caden 正在做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can see what Lewis is working on.
zh: 我可以看到 Lewis 正在做什么。

en: I can see what Tywin is working on.

en: And I can see Jackson's face pop up there.

speaker: Unknown
en: I can click in and see what he's working on in real time.
zh: 我可以点进去，实时查看他正在做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think collaboration is
zh: 而且我觉得协作是

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the most important new concepts in these tools that no one is really talking about right now.
zh: 这些工具中最重要的新概念之一，而现在没有人在真正谈论它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Collaboration is important because not only is it true that all great things are built with teams of people.
zh: 协作很重要，因为不仅所有伟大的东西都是由团队的人构建的这一点是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're not built by individuals.
zh: 它们不是由个人构建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're built by teams.

en: The final principle that I want to talk about today, and the title of this talk is Orchestras, Not Factories.
zh: 今天我想谈的最后一个原则,也是这次演讲的标题,是「管弦乐团,而不是工厂」。

speaker: Unknown
en: The whole talk track today is about software factories, and I honestly kind of hate the term.
zh: 今天整场演讲的主线都是关于软件工厂的,而说实话我有点讨厌这个词。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's the wrong way of thinking about these new tools that are emerging.
zh: 我认为这是对正在涌现的这些新工具的一种错误的思考方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I think of a factory, I think of automation, and I think of, there's a lot of amazing things about automation, and it makes our lives more efficient, and we can create more of everything.
zh: 当我想到工厂时,我想到的是自动化,而自动化有很多了不起的地方,它让我们的生活更高效,我们可以创造更多的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't want the future to be built around factories.
zh: 我不希望未来是围绕工厂构建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want the future to, I want to feel like a human.
zh: 我希望未来,我希望感觉自己是一个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to be in the flow.
zh: 我想要处于心流之中。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to be in front of an orchestra, waving my baton, and I wave it this way, and this team of agents starts working, and then this intermingling of humans and agents starts working as I go here.
zh: 我想站在一个管弦乐团面前,挥舞着我的指挥棒,我朝这边一挥,这支智能体团队就开始工作,然后随着我继续指挥,这种人类与智能体交织的协作就开始运转。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when I want to, I can zoom in on the details, but most of the time I can zoom out.
zh: 而当我想的时候,我可以放大看细节,但大多数时候我可以缩小视野。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't think the future should be we are like managing swarms of agents and we are like factory line managers like pushing buttons, getting the agents to like pump out the next feature.
zh: 我不认为未来应该是我们像管理智能体集群一样,像流水线管理员一样按按钮,让智能体去产出下一个功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we tried this like 10 years ago with the term feature factories and it just doesn't work.
zh: 就像我们大约 10 年前用「功能工厂」这个术语尝试过的那样,那根本行不通。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I want my software to feel human and crafted.
zh: 我希望我的软件感觉像人的、有匠心的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to feel like a human at the center of it all.
zh: 我想感觉自己是一个处于这一切中心的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think because we're all building these tools we actually have a responsibility
zh: 而且我认为,因为我们都在构建这些工具,我们实际上有一份责任

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's really important to use the words that make us feel excited and feel capable and feel like we're in the flow and having fun.

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I don't think the future is something like this.
zh: 所以我认为未来不应该是像这样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't want to be in my dark factory.
zh: 我不想待在我的黑暗工厂里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't want to be a line manager.
zh: 我不想成为一名流水线管理员。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to feel like this.
zh: 我想感觉像这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to be in the flow.
zh: 我想处于心流之中。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to be having fun.
zh: 我想享受乐趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to be crafting things.
zh: 我想打磨创造东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to feel like I'm Steve Jobs designing the Mac with a team of amazing humans and AI agents all in the same place.
zh: 我想感觉自己像 Steve Jobs,和一群了不起的人类以及 AI 智能体一起,在同一个地方设计 Mac。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to feel like I'm in an orchestra.
zh: 我想让自己感觉像身处一个管弦乐团。

speaker: Unknown
en: So here are my principles for being the best builder in your organization.
zh: 这就是我对成为你所在组织中最好的构建者的几条原则。

speaker: Unknown
en: Stay near the frontier, don't try and beat the market, create slot-free zones, feed the beast, free-range agents, and think about orchestras, not factories.
zh: 靠近前沿，不要试图打败市场，创造无槽区域，喂养野兽，放养智能体，思考管弦乐团而不是工厂。

speaker: Unknown
en: I came up with this handy acronym for remembering it, STICFO.
zh: 我为了方便记住这些想了个缩写，STICFO。

en: All right, so thanks a ton for having me.

en: I'll be around.

speaker: Unknown
en: Feel free to ask questions, and I'll see you on the internet.
zh: 欢迎随时提问，我们网上见。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。
